description: Governance patterns for orgs where Apex triggers and record-triggered Flows both run on the same object: field-write conflict prevention, single-entry-point consolidation, recursion guards across automation types, and automation inventory. Use when inheriting a mixed-automation org, adding a Flow to an object that already has triggers, or resolving silent field-overwrite bugs. NOT for save order of execution — use apex/order-of-execution-deep-dive. NOT for Flow-only patterns — use flow/record-triggered-flow-patterns.
inputs: Object name and list of all active automations (triggers, flows, workflow rules, process builder)
Description of the field-write conflict or recursion symptom
Whether the org has a single-trigger-per-object pattern or multiple triggers
name: trigger-and-flow-coexistence
official_sources: Apex Developer Guide: Triggers and Order of Execution (20-step list; before-save Flows step 3, before triggers step 4) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm
Metadata API Developer Guide: Flow (`triggerOrder`, API 54.0+) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_visual_workflow.htm
Salesforce Help: Record-Triggered Automation Decision Guide — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_trigger.htm

Corpus cites (2026-10-20): order of execution steps 3-4 (salesforce_apex_developer_guide.txt 264 L15643-15644), validation step 5 (L15645-15646), workflow re-fire once and no flow re-run (L15654-15662), steps 12-14 (L15664-15673), multiple triggers per event not ordered (L15705-15707), at API 53.0 and earlier after-save flows run after entitlements (L15712)
outputs: Automation inventory matrix documenting every automation on the object, its type, timing, and field writes
Conflict analysis identifying field-write collisions and execution-order risks
Refactoring plan to eliminate or guard against coexistence problems
